sections.title: Positioning
sections.body: iCoolKJ Platform is a Source Available general-purpose foundation for enterprise admin systems, published for non-commercial study and research.

sections.title: Where it fits
sections.body: When you need unified users, tenants, permissions, workflow, audit, and engineering norms, a foundation beats building from scratch.
bullets: Admin consoles and internal business systems
SaaS back offices and multi-customer operations
Ticket, approval, knowledge, and CRM-style workflow systems
Regulated projects needing security governance and domestic-stack readiness

sections.title: Core goals
sections.body: One foundation for many projects: platform capabilities sink down, business modules float up, with a unified stack and initialization baseline.
bullets: Reuse one foundation across projects
Governable out of the box: tenants, orgs, RBAC, security, audit
Non-commercial study and research use
Multi-tenant design with long-term maintainability

sections.title: Vs packaged SaaS / greenfield builds
sections.body: Compared with packaged SaaS, you can read and modify every layer. Compared with greenfield, you can study a working implementation of auth, tenancy, and audit.

categories.title: Capabilities
categories.summary: Deliverable-oriented capabilities: tenancy, RBAC, workflow, codegen, async import, and operations.

sections.title: Multi-tenant & org permissions
sections.body: One account per tenant with clear platform vs tenant boundaries; departments, posts, roles, and data scope for enterprise-style orgs.

sections.title: Menus, RBAC & security
sections.body: Navigation separated from permission codes (directory / menu / button). Login lockout, captcha, IP rules, password policy, and log redaction are configurable.

sections.title: Workflow & OA
sections.body: Process design, runtime approvals, and tenant office configuration for real leave/expense-style workloads.

sections.title: Codegen & engineering norms
sections.body: CRUD generation and consistent front/back structure to accelerate standard admin modules.

sections.title: Async jobs & Excel import/export
sections.body: Sync Excel import covers light workloads; async import stages the file, returns a task id immediately, and lets the UI poll results—so large files do not block HTTP threads. Business async tasks (infra_async_task) stay separate from platform cron (sys_job). Transport is environment config (in-process or dedicated worker)—tenants never pick the channel—while each task keeps tenant and owner ownership. Codegen can emit async import APIs and handlers.

sections.title: i18n & configuration
sections.body: Shell, business copy, and menu titles support locales; config, dictionaries, and tenant policy seams stay clear.

sections.title: Deploy, ops & domestic stack
sections.body: Initialization baselines, backup, scheduled jobs, and online sessions for production. Middleware abstractions ease regulated migrations.

categories.title: Security & compliance
categories.summary: For security and enterprise evaluators: demonstrable, configurable controls (not a certification claim).

sections.title: How to read this
sections.body: This summarizes application-side capabilities that can be configured or demonstrated. Application alignment is not a classified-protection pass; network, host, and policy evidence still belong to deployment and operations.

sections.title: Authentication
sections.body: Password complexity and history, expiry, login lockout and IP throttling, optional captcha; TOTP MFA for administrators with tenant-level force-enroll.

sections.title: Access control
sections.body: RBAC with tenant isolation and data scope; IP rules where platform deny overrides tenant allow; separation-of-duty role templates with mutual exclusion.

sections.title: Security audit
sections.body: Login, operation, and API access logs with sensitive-field masking; hash-chain integrity and in-DB archival retention; no casual delete APIs on audit trails.

sections.title: Session & transport hardening
sections.body: JWT + Redis sessions, opaque refresh rotation, single-session policy and forced logout; CORS allowlist and security headers; Swagger off in production profiles.

sections.title: Tenant-owned security policy
sections.body: Platform sets defaults; tenant admins may override login, password, captcha, and MFA policies within their scope.

categories.title: Solutions
categories.summary: Map common scenarios to pain points, approach, and deliverables.

sections.title: Multi-tenant SaaS operations
sections.body: Provision tenants, admins, and policy baselines; each tenant manages orgs, roles, and data in isolation on one console.
bullets: Pain: one stack per customer is costly; auth/audit hard to unify
Approach: shared schema + tenant_id isolation + tenant policy overrides
Deliverables: provisioning, admin accounts, defaults, runbooks

sections.title: Group & subsidiary administration
sections.body: Enterprise and organization tenants, region trees, and org structures support group-to-unit models with scoped permissions.

sections.title: Approval / OA mid-platform
sections.body: Hang workflow and forms on unified users and orgs; tenants configure office templates instead of rebuilding engines per line of business.

sections.title: Incubate new admin products faster
sections.body: Ship standard CRUD modules via codegen while auth, permissions, audit, and i18n come from the foundation.

sections.title: Domestic-stack migration path
sections.body: Replace DB, cache, and file adapters behind abstractions—pilot by swapping implementations, not rewriting business layers.

bullets: This project is Source Available under a non-commercial study and research licence. Commercial use is prohibited. It is NOT OSI Open Source.
Multi-tenant? Yes—one account per tenant with clear boundaries.
Domestic stack? Middleware abstractions are designed for adapter swaps.
